[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Johne and Issobel Glasgow were baptized on 03-Feb-1648 in Mid Calder parish. They were the children of [[Glasgow-2453|William Glasgow]]. As they were baptized on the same day, they were probably twins. 

Isobel was born in 1648. She is the daughter of [[Glasgow-3515|William Glasgow]].
<ref>
"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BV-Z9H : 12 February 2020), Issobell Glasgow, 1648.
</ref>

== Research Notes ==
A possible identification concerns Isob Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Isob Glasgow and James Coldwell/ on 17 April 1684 at Glasgow.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 644 / 1/230 / 285; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. Isob Glasgow and James Coldwell have no proven compatible local/live identity. The identification remains uncertain.

=== Possible earlier Haddington record ===

A Haddington transcript records Issobell Glasgow born on 24 November 1639 and baptised on 26 November, with parents named Wm Glasgow and Issobella Miral.<ref name="EarlyHaddington1639">Findmypast/Scottish Genealogy Society, Issobell Glasgow, born 24 and baptised 26 November 1639, Haddington; OPR 709/1 p.208, transcript SCOT/OPR/BAP/4675742; original register not inspected; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4675742].</ref> Miral is the literal provider reading; the original maternal surname has not been checked.

This is a possible earlier record of the Issobell baptised at Mid Calder on 3 February 1648: the child’s name and father William agree, and a baptism date does not independently prove a birthday. The nine-year interval and different parish nevertheless make the identity weak; a second or delayed baptism is a possibility rather than a recorded explanation. The Haddington entry directly proves its own indexed parental pair, without identifying its father with [[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow of Mid Calder]]. [[Glasgow-3075|William Glasgow, the Leith mealmaker]], and [[Glasgow-3517|William Glasgow, the Inveresk child of 1614]], are separate compatible adult comparisons. None is made the Haddington father as a fact. [[Anderson-56713|Issobell Anderson]], who married Allexander Glasgow at Edinburgh in 1665, represents a different birth-surname account; she is not identified with this Glasgow-born child merely from her later married name.
